analyst_view.overall: Leaders Lazio (29 points, unbeaten) host Lecce (14th, 10 points, one win in five), who need points to stay clear of the bottom three. Zaccagni, Nuno Tavares, Sutalo and Marusic are still out, as the numbers assume, and Doekhi has a hand problem; what changed since this morning is that Gattuso said Frattesi trained all week and is fine (only a possible cold to check), and that several players who have had little time will start, with Cataldi carrying a minor adductor issue. For Lecce, Di Francesco said Monteiro has recovered and could even start, and he is in the 26-man squad, although the numbers still count him as out; Pierotti is ruled out and Berisha is back but not sharp. Referee Matteo Marcenaro's high card rate (4.5 a game) is already in the numbers. With Frattesi fit, Monteiro back and some Lazio rotation pulling the other way, I drop this morning's small cuts and stay with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals, already cut for Zaccagni (-10.5%) and Tavares and for Monteiro (-5% on Lecce's side). Changed: Frattesi is fit, so this morning's -3% goes, and Monteiro is back and may start, which gives Lecce a little more than the numbers think, while Gattuso's plan to start some less-used players takes a little off Lazio; those roughly cancel, so I stay at about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Without Zaccagni and Tavares Lazio lose their most direct left side, while Lecce have won plenty of corners lately (33 in six) and get winger Monteiro back; the numbers already see the absences and the form, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards and already add Marcenaro's high rate (+19%) while taking some off for Lazio's calm recent run. Di Francesco wants a brave Lecce that presses without fear, which can bring fouls, but there is no rivalry or suspension threat, so I stay at about 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.7 shots. Changed: Frattesi, Lazio's midfielder who shoots most from deep, is fit, so I drop this morning's -2%; Gattuso's partial rotation and Lecce's front three getting Monteiro back pull in opposite directions, so I stay at about 25.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target, with Lecce's sharp recent shooting (34 on target in six) already counted. With Frattesi available again this morning's -3% goes, and nothing else in the team news moves the total, so I stay at about 8.7.
